nodes.label: Greek philosophy & Platonism
nodes.blurb: Plato's philosophy and the schools that grew from it.

nodes.label: Platonism
nodes.blurb: Socrates, Pythagoras and Plato: the soul, the Forms and philosophy as preparation for death.

nodes.label: Neoplatonism
nodes.blurb: Plotinus, Porphyry, Iamblichus and Proclus: emanation from the One and the return of the soul.

nodes.label: Renaissance Platonism
nodes.blurb: Ficino and the Florentine revival of Plato and Plotinus.

nodes.label: Christian mysticism
nodes.blurb: Dionysius, Eckhart, Porete and Böhme to Centering Prayer and today's contemplative teachers.

nodes.label: Western esotericism
nodes.blurb: Gnosticism, Hermeticism, Theosophy, Anthroposophy and the Fourth Way.

nodes.label: Gnosticism
nodes.blurb: Salvation through gnosis: the Nag Hammadi texts, Sethians and Valentinians.

nodes.label: Theosophy
nodes.blurb: Blavatsky's Theosophical Society (1875) and its teachings on karma and reincarnation. Wikidata is the Society item.

nodes.label: Anthroposophy
nodes.blurb: Rudolf Steiner's spiritual science, which split from the Theosophical Society in 1912–13.

nodes.label: The Fourth Way
nodes.blurb: Gurdjieff's Work: waking from sleep through self-remembering, carried on by Ouspensky and the Gurdjieff Foundations.

nodes.label: Independent teachers
nodes.blurb: Teachers outside any tradition or lineage.

nodes.label: Krishnamurti
nodes.blurb: J. Krishnamurti's teaching after he left Theosophy in 1929: no path, no authority, freedom from the known.
